x-handover.name: assembly outputs and QC results
x-handover.source: Anil Wipat, bioprospecting use case slides, dbtl-synbio/dbtlhub, 10 Nov 2026
x-handover.note: The use case numbers its handovers. Carrying that number in the contract means two teams arguing about 'the Design handover' are provably arguing about the same one.

title: Build -> Test handover (generic)
description: The common ground for both use cases: every test item traces back to a Design item and to a physical location, every measurement carries its own unit and method, and the target list is inherited from Design. What differs between bioprospecting and biomanufacturing is bound by a profile - identifier patterns, container vocabulary, and which measurements are mandatory. Fields marked x-pattern take their regex from the active profile.

profile.description: Which use-case profile this package was written against.

produced_by.description: Who produced this package. 'engine' records the model used, or 'none' for a deterministic step - this is what makes the model comparison fall out of the ledger.

design_ref.description: The link back to Design. 'items' is what Design committed to; every sample must trace to one of them. In bioprospecting an item is an enzyme candidate, in biomanufacturing a pathway construct - the structure is the same.

accession.description: Resolvable, prefixed identifier - the shared backbone (MetaNetX / identifiers.org style).

target_list.description: Inherited from Design: what Test is expected to measure. The enzyme substrate/product in bioprospecting, the pathway product in biomanufacturing. InChIKey is mandatory either way, so the Test phase can resolve what it is looking for.

location.description: Where the material physically is. A plate well, a vial, a flask, a bioreactor port - the profile fixes the vocabulary, the structure does not change.

measurements.description: The common ground. A number on its own is not a measurement: quantity, value, unit and method travel together, always. This is the generalisation of 'peak area is not flux'.

unit.description: Use 'dimensionless' rather than omitting the field; 'none' is not a unit.

method.description: The instrument or procedure that produced the number.

not_delivered.description: Items Design committed to that are not in this plate, each with a reason. A failed synthesis is a normal outcome and belongs here; what is not acceptable is a well that is simply absent from the record, because then nobody can tell a failure from an omission.

reason.description: What happened, in the vendor's or the lab's own words.

reads.description: Crates or packages this handover READ but did not produce. Information in this framework normally flows one way, from the phase that made something to the phase that receives it. This is the other direction: a receiving phase states what it can do, and the sending phase has to have looked. Referenced, never inlined - the package stays small and the graph joins the crates by their identifiers.

role.description: constraints: limits this package had to respect. context: read to interpret something. upstream: where the material came from.

checksum.description: Which version was read. A shared crate grows between rounds, so 'the Build crate' is not a unique thing to have read.

limits.description: Limits this package was built to respect, lifted out of the crates named in 'reads'. Carried here rather than left in the crate so that a check can compare against them, and 'from' says which crate each one came out of. A limit is not a use-case constant and does not belong in the profile: it is this run's equipment and this round's budget, and it changes between rounds.

from.description: The crate this limit was read out of.

stated_by.description: Who or what put it there - a researcher seeding the crate before round 1, or a phase recording its own equipment.

x-dbtl-checks.message: two samples claim the same physical position
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: re-read the liquid handler worklist. Guessing which sample sat where would fabricate a lab record

x-dbtl-checks.message: this item is not in what Design committed to
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: either Design adds the item, or Build mislabelled the sample
not auto-fixable: a measurement that was never taken cannot be supplied. Either the instrument output is found, or the sample is reported as incomplete

x-dbtl-checks.message: Design committed to this item and the Build record neither contains it nor reports it as not delivered
x-dbtl-checks.fix_hint: not auto-fixable: an absent well has no field to correct. Either the sample is found and added, or the failure is stated in not_delivered. Dropping it silently is how a failed synthesis becomes a missing result nobody can explain.
